# the contributor audit of radius saturation and whole-cap section profiles



## Central-ray monotonicity: PASS

Read `candidate 83b3822a403eee2c` in full. In canonical coordinates the diagonal cancellation is correct, and increasing a radius raises precisely its diagonal and adjacent off-diagonal entries. The finite endpoint bounds are exactly the adjacent core inequalities, so the new matrix remains a Z-matrix. Entrywise domination of a PSD Z-matrix by another Z-matrix implies PSD by the displayed absolute-value quadratic-form comparison. This argument does not require positive definiteness, positive excess, or a limiting body. The independently audited exact realization criterion supplies a body at the closed upper endpoint.

Opposite radii do not occur in each other's bounds and have disjoint incident edges, even for two central lines. Their sequential or simultaneous saturation is valid. The target normalized reciprocal chord weight strictly decreases upon any actual increase, with every area-only constraint fixed. The four canonical saturated pairs are correctly listed. This is a finite-data/global optimization reduction, with no unsupported claim about Hausdorff-local replacement of an arbitrary original body.

For arbitrary central arrangements the next-neighbor angular gap is at most pi: the distinct consecutive gaps over a semicircle sum to pi, and any two adjacent gaps form a subcollection of these. Equality occurs for two lines. The coefficient c_i is therefore nonnegative, so the diagonal monotonicity persists; all determinant and core factors in the general formulas are correct. No statement about other caps or neighboring mixed fibers is implied.

## Positive-definite optimizer exclusion, including zero excess: PASS

Read the updated Theorem 2 of `historical context (not an accepted premise)`. Decreasing one positive radius on a different chord decreases its two incident determinants and preserves every core inequality, including equality. Positive definiteness persists for a sufficiently small perturbation by continuity. Realization then gives an admissible body with the target numerator fixed and a strictly larger reciprocal-chord denominator. Thus no finite-data local or global-body minimum can have a positive-definite matrix. The proof does not require strict sector excess; strict excess is only required for the separately proved unique-polygon rigidity conclusion. This supersedes the formerly pending zero-excess audit in `historical context (not an accepted premise)`.

## Whole-cap supremal section profile: PASS

Read `candidate 443fb78ca8dd4f80` in full. The initial shear sends both actual endpoint centroids to zero, preserves the lattice and fiber measure, and transports all ambient halfspaces. The endpoint thresholds alpha and minus alpha have the correct signs. Every nonempty pair of endpoint sections contributes a contained Minkowski average to the actual middle section. Brunn--Minkowski in the transverse subspace applies also to nonempty zero-volume sections. Restricting the allocation to the actual closed projection intervals is necessary and is explicitly done.

The section roots are continuous on the closed intervals with their actual endpoint values. On the interior this is concavity. At an endpoint, convex interpolation from an endpoint section gives the lower-limit inequality; compactness and upper semicontinuity of sections give the reverse upper-limit inequality. Thus the allocation supremum is attained. Concavity, bounded support, and Fubini justify the integral. The resulting sum concerns one actual oblique cap, not separately optimized caps.

Replacing transverse sections by concentric equal-volume balls yields actual convex bodies. Their midpoint section is the union of concentric balls indexed by the compact allocation set, so its volume equals the supremal profile exactly. Volume and the axial first moment are preserved; symmetry sets every transverse first moment to zero. This proves directional sharpness, without preserving unrelated directions.

The axial triangular profiles have the stated support and area. Their midpoint roof has the two stated slopes, total area (R+1)/2, and the stated positive and negative cap areas. The positive endpoint sum has a proper stationary cut and lower value than any full-cap transition. The negative-direction sum is concave on every proper-state interval, so its extrema reduce to the explicitly compared supporting transitions. The two factored excesses and positivity conditions are correct. The independent exact verifier returned PASS for 18,304 checks.

The general tent parameterization and finite quadratic tilt-minimization list include all proper, tangent, empty, and full statuses, with coincident breakpoints and the endpoint tent modes handled explicitly. The all-parameter inequality remains unproved; only the two common-axis slices are used as theorems.
